title: The service table shows Service, Interval, Canned Lines and reorders
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in as an Owner/Admin, or a user with "Settings Service" enabled, on the build under test. The Maintenance Reminders feature is on for the shop (it ships behind the maintenance_reminders flag).
  2. In the left sidebar under Settings choose "Maintenance" (it sits beneath "Inspection Templates"). Schedules here belong to the location chosen in the header.
  3. A schedule open in the editor with at least two services - one with several triggers, one whose lines include absorbed lines. Seed it:
  4. ↳ New schedule -> Add service "PM-A" (calendar Every 3 months + a mileage trigger e.g. 15,000 mileage) with several canned lines.
  5. ↳ Add service "PM-C" that covers PM-A (so some of its lines are absorbed).
custom_steps:
1. Read the service table columns and how the Interval and Canned Lines cells render.
  2. Reorder services by drag, then by Move up / Move down.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Services are listed as a table with columns Service, Interval and Canned Lines.
  • The Interval cell shows each trigger separated by a dot, never "or" (e.g. "15,000 mileage - 3 months" or "30 days"); the Canned Lines cell shows the line count and any absorption (e.g. "4 lines - 3 absorbed").
  • Services reorder by drag and by Move up / Move down.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-3780 (Maintenance Reminders); story SV-10558 (S1, Create a maintenance schedule); Chunk 1 MR spec (Confluence 886931488), Part 1 / S1; read 29 Sep 2026. Source-verified 29 September 2026; not yet build-verified.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S1-R9: “Services are listed as a table: Service, Interval and Canned Lines. The interval renders each trigger separated by a dot, never by or, for example 15,000 mileage · 3 months, or 30 days, and the canned-lines cell carries the line count and any absorption, for example 4 lines · 3 absorbed”
  • S1-R10: “Services will be reorderable by drag and by Move up / Move down”
